alpaca.origin: The alpaca is a domestic South American camelid. Mitochondrial and microsatellite analysis by Kadwell and colleagues (2001) indicates that it descends from the wild vicuna rather than the guanaco, and they proposed the binomial Vicugna pacos; earlier work cited in that study dated domestication to about 6,000 to 7,000 years ago in the Peruvian Andes. Two fleece types are bred, Huacaya and Suri, and fleece type is reported to be controlled by a single dominant gene. Much published breeding data comes from the Pacomarca experimental farm of the Peruvian firm Inca Tops.
alpaca.structure: Alpaca fiber is alpha-keratin with a cuticle of thin overlapping scales around a cortex, but unlike fine Merino wool a substantial share of fibers carries a medulla. Camelid laboratories classify fibers as non-medullated, fragmented, discontinuous, continuous or strongly medullated, and medullation rises with diameter. Reported mean fiber diameters span roughly 18 to 36 microns. Suri and Huacaya also differ at the surface: in a Peruvian comparison, Suri fleece had the highest share of fibers with fewer than eight cuticular scales per 100 microns of length, consistent with its smooth, lustrous locks, whereas Huacaya is selected for density and crimp.
alpaca.process: Research on follicle development shows that the secondary follicle population matures early in life, which supports an early first shearing. Shorn fleeces are skirted and then sorted by hand into fineness grades and natural colors, because diameter varies across body regions within a single fleece. Sorted fiber is scoured, carded and either combed into top for worsted yarn or spun on the woollen route. Coarse and medullated fibers cause prickle, so processors blend or remove them to limit the share of fibers above about 30 microns, while breeding programs attack the same problem upstream by selecting on mean diameter, its variation and medullation.
alpaca.performance: Like other keratin fibers, alpaca absorbs water vapor, chars and self-extinguishes rather than melting, and takes acid and metal-complex dyes on its amino groups; its wide range of natural colors means much yarn is sold undyed. Comfort depends more on the diameter distribution and medullation of a lot than on the animal name: medullated fibers resist bending and compression, raise the prickle factor, and look chalky beside dyed neighbors. Suri drapes and shines, while crimped Huacaya gives loft. The fiber is vulnerable to clothes moth and carpet beetle larvae and to strongly alkaline detergents.
alpaca.identify: Burn tests (indicative only, and to be done with care) show the burnt-hair smell and crushable ash of any keratin. Projection microscopy prepared under IWTO-8 and newer automated image systems measure diameter and classify medullation, and cuticular scale counts help separate Suri, Huacaya and llama fiber. For species, spectroscopy works better: a forensic study found infrared spectroscopy identified alpaca but could not separate vicuna from guanaco, while ambient-ionization mass spectrometry resolved all three. ATR-FTIR with chemometrics has also discriminated alpaca from cashmere, mohair, yak, camel, vicuna, llama and sheep fibers.
alpaca.labeling: In the US, the Wool Products Labeling Act of 1939 includes alpaca among the specialty fibers that fall within the statutory definition of wool, so the specialty fiber name may be used in place of the word wool with its percentage, and FTC rules exclude alpaca from the catch-all term fur fiber. In the EU, Annex I of Regulation (EU) No 1007/2011 lists alpaca among the fine animal hairs, followed or not by the word wool or hair. Textile Exchange's Responsible Alpaca Standard is a voluntary welfare and land-management certification; buyers should confirm that a certificate covers the specific product.
alpaca.past: Andean camelids were nearly extirpated during the Spanish conquest, one reason the ancestry of alpaca and llama was long disputed; genetic analysis also revealed extensive hybridization between the two domestic forms. Modern alpaca improvement concentrates on fiber. The International Committee for Animal Recording recommends mean fiber diameter and its coefficient of variation as the first traits in breeding programs, and heritability studies from Pacomarca have added medullation as a selection criterion to reduce prickle. Genomic scans of that selected population now reveal selection signatures near hair-follicle genes. Alpacas are also kept in Europe for fiber and tourism, raising husbandry and welfare questions outside the Andes.
